item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00084","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C12","C17","C23"],"selected_candidate_label":"C12","confidence":0.82,"relationship_type":"both","rationale":"C12 is a plausible direct precursor: it is a recent letter to the same Federal Works Administrator concerning disaster relief, expressly praises Fleming's efforts to “coordinate disaster relief,” identifies the danger of inadequate relief for stricken communities, and calls for consideration of a permanent arrangement. The child converts those ideas into concrete instructions for Fleming to coordinate all Federal agencies, supplement existing assistance, investigate the disaster, and recommend any needed legislation. This shared addressee, distinctive disaster-coordination language, and progression from considering permanent arrangements to directing coordinated action constitute material drafting evidence. C17 shares the study-and-report machinery but concerns an unrelated policy field; C23 has only weaker parallels involving immediate action and interagency liaison.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"I am directing you to coordinate the efforts of all Federal agencies in alleviating hardship and suffering caused by this disaster.","parent_excerpt":"I want to thank you for your consistent efforts to coordinate disaster relief.","explanation":"Distinctive shared language assigns the same official a disaster-relief coordination role."},{"child_excerpt":"make an immediate investigation and report to me the facts concerning the disaster and any recommendations you deem appropriate concerning the need for additional legislative authority","parent_excerpt":"the Disaster Surplus Property Program may not provide adequate relief to stricken communities in the future... We should now give consideration to making a permanent arrangement for disaster relief.","explanation":"The child operationalizes C12's concern about inadequate future relief and permanent arrangements through an investigation, recommendations, and possible legislation."},{"child_excerpt":"The Housing and Home Finance Agency and the Corps of Engineers are already rendering emergency assistance, but their efforts can and should be supplemented by those of other Federal agencies.","parent_excerpt":"the danger that the Disaster Surplus Property Program may not provide adequate relief to stricken communities in the future","explanation":"Both frame existing federal relief mechanisms as potentially inadequate and requiring broader or more durable federal action."}]}
